explanation: In Ovid's telling, the wine god Bacchus granted the wish. When even his food turned to metal, Midas washed the gift away in the river Pactolus, whose sands then glittered with gold.

claims.text: In Greek myth, King Midas was granted a wish that turned everything he touched into gold.
In the myth, Midas's touch turns things to gold, not to silver, bronze or glass.
In Ovid's Metamorphoses, the god Bacchus (Dionysus) grants Midas his wish.
In Ovid's account, Midas's food turns to gold, and he is freed by washing in the river Pactolus, whose sands then carry gold.
